title: Costs, Lessons and Further Safeguards Arising from Recent Disruptions to Digital Banking Services
what_it_is: Costs, Lessons and Further Safeguards Arising from Recent Disruptions to Digital Banking Services

sections.label: Questions on digital banking outages
sections.summary: Questions asked whether MAS will impose accountability measures, require compensation, and regulate data centre providers after DBS and Citibank disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister whether MAS will consider (i) imposing user-centric accountability measures on banks such as the requirement to publish service reliability reports of digital banking services and proactively engage customers on service recovery and alternative options during outages and (ii) requiring banks to compensate their banking customers who suffer financial losses due to outages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister with regard to the disruption to the digital banking services of DBS and Citibank on 14 October 2023 (a) whether MAS has any data on how many (i) customers and (ii) businesses have been affected; and (b) whether local banks are required to maintain robust levels of redundancy in critical banking infrastructure such as the data centre that is maintained by third-party service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what lessons can be drawn from the recent disruptions to digital banking services of DBS and Citibank, in view that these occurred despite MAS' tightened Business Continuity Management (BCM) guidelines for financial institutions to better manage such disruptions; (b) whether MAS will consider regulating data centre service providers that serve major financial institutions in Singapore; and (c) how does MAS plan to tighten the oversight of its BCM guidelines on financial institutions in Singapore.

sections.label: Failed access and transaction figures
sections.summary: Up to 810,000 access attempts failed and about 2.5 million payment and ATM transactions could not be completed during the disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Up to 810,000 attempts to access the digital banking platforms of both banks were estimated to have failed between 2.54 pm on 14 October 2023 and 4.47 am on 15 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Approximately 2.5 million payment and ATM transactions could not be completed.

sections.label: MAS operational risk multiplier
sections.summary: In May 2023, MAS imposed a 1.8 times multiplier to DBS' risk weighted assets for operational risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In May 2023, in response to repeated outages, MAS imposed a multiplier of 1.8 times to DBS' risk weighted assets for operational risk.

sections.label: DBS remediation restrictions imposed
sections.summary: MAS prohibited DBS from non-essential IT changes or new business ventures for six months and barred branch and ATM network reductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The review was completed in August and DBS has set out a technology resiliency roadmap to address the findings and to improve system resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To ensure that DBS keeps a sharp focus on restoring the resilience of its digital banking services, MAS has prohibited DBS from making any non-essential IT changes or acquiring any new business ventures for a six-month period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS has also barred DBS from reducing the size of its branch and ATM networks in Singapore until MAS is satisfied with the progress of DBS' remediation.

sections.label: Restrictions on DBS changes
sections.summary: DBS is not allowed to make IT changes, make acquisitions, or decrease the number of physical ATMs and branches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The bank, or DBS in this case, is not allowed to make any IT changes and also to involve themselves in any acquisitions, and the third, is that they are not to decrease the number of physical ATMs and branches.

sections.label: Impact of regulatory capital
sections.summary: Imposition of regulatory capital will impact banks, drag on return of capital, and could affect credit ratings and stock price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, through MAS' actions – which I mentioned and went into detail on – how imposition of regulatory capital will impact the banks; in addition, it will be a drag on the return of capital, it could impact their credit ratings and it could impact their stock price.

sections.label: Bank year-end compensation process
sections.summary: The bank will reflect this in its year-end compensation process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The bank will reflect this in its year-end compensation process.

sections.label: MAS actions against Citibank
sections.summary: MAS will assess supervisory actions against Citibank after the 14 October investigations and incorporate learnings into banks' risk controls and its 2024 exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Second, for Citibank, MAS will assess the supervisory actions to be taken against Citibank following the conclusions of the investigations in the 14 October incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS will work with financial industry to incorporate the key learnings from this incident into all banks' risk management controls and include it into the MAS' future tech supervisory approach and also discuss it and it will be a key measure for the next financial sector business continuity exercise in 2024.

sections.label: Data centre resilience and MAS
sections.summary: MAS will work with authorities on data centre policy and expects financial institutions to implement risk controls for data centre resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As we know, data centres serve multiple industries, not just the financial sector, MAS will, indeed, work with the relevant authorities on the Government's policy over data centre reliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But let me also assure Members that although MAS does not directly regulate data centres, MAS expects all financial institutions to implement adequate risk controls to ensure data centre resilience such as conducting a threat and vulnerability risk assessment to identify potential vulnerabilities and weaknesses and the protection that they should establish to safeguard data centres against physical and environmental threats.

sections.label: Waived late charges and DBS restrictions
sections.summary: DBS and Citibank will waive late charges from the outage, and restrictions on DBS activities aim to let it fix issues from 14 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To Ms Jean's point also, for customers who incurred late charges due to the outrage, DBS and Citibank will waive these charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To Mr Don Wee's question, in fact, I had already explained that the point of restricting some of these activities, either acquisitions or reduce the scale-back of ATMs and branches and restricting the IT changes, these are all meant for this particular period for the bank, for DBS, to focus on remediating and fixing the issues that led to 14 October and, in fact, other issues that have related to the multiple disruptions over the course of a year.
